## Summary

`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` / `ensure_claimed()` in
`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` compare the item's current status against
the string `"in_progress"`, but the `wl` CLI stores and returns statuses in
hyphenated form (`"in-progress"`). Consequently:

- `require_claimed()` **always raises `ClaimError`** for genuinely claimed
  items (observed while running `/skill:plan SA-0MTYJ5VFI003PZMI`: item
  status `"in-progress"` failed the `!= "in_progress"` guard). The
  SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 fail-closed guard is therefore non-functional in
  production.
- `ensure_claimed()` never recognises an existing claim, so it performs a
  redundant `wl update --status in_progress` write on every call instead of
  being a read-only no-op.

Root cause check: `wl` (ContextHub `dist/commands/update.js`) explicitly
normalises underscore → hyphen on write ("stored statuses are (underscore →
hyphen) so `in_progress` matches the stored `in-progress`"), and the same
package's `show` returns `"in-progress"` in JSON. The unit tests in
`test_status_lifecycle.py` mock `wl show` responses with `status="in_progress"`
(underscore), so they never exercise the real CLI's hyphenated value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `require_claimed()` passes when the stored status is `"in-progress"` (hyphen) and fails closed only when it is genuinely not claimed.
- [ ] `ensure_claimed()` is a read-only no-op when the stored status is already `"in-progress"` (no `wl update` write).
- [ ] Unit tests assert behaviour against the hyphenated stored value (matching `wl show` output), in addition to any underscore variants.
- [ ] Full test suite passes.

## Incident Summary

The local `dev` branch of this repository points at a destructive commit `2c30dbfe` (message "init", author `T <t@t.com>`) that deletes 472 files / 138,007 lines and replaces the repo root with 5 placeholder files (`install.sh`, `remote`, `sshl`, `update`, `ai.home.conf`) plus `tests/test_a.py`. The local main checkout currently has no code (e.g. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and the test suite are gone).

## Evidence (collected 2026-09-19 11:56 IST)

- `git rev-parse HEAD` = `2c30dbfe` (`init`, T <t@t.com>, Sat Sep 19 07:01:18 2026 +0100), parent `27e0f905` (real dev commit).
- `git diff --numstat 27e0f905 2c30dbfe`: 472 files changed, 6 insertions, 138,007 deletions.
- `git ls-tree --name-only HEAD` returns only: ai.home.conf, install.sh, remote, sshl, tests/test_a.py, update.
- Local `dev` reflog: `2c30dbfe dev@{0}: pull origin dev: Fast-forward` — the destructive commit was pulled into the main checkout (~07:23) from origin.
- The working tree has been actively changing during this session: the file `skill/audit/tests/test_budget_exceeded_resume.py` existed and ran green at session start, then vanished mid-session as the pull landed.
- `origin/dev` (live `git ls-remote` = `74bd0437 fix: resolve 9 code quality findings across 5 files (SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK)`) is INTACT: full tree (`pytest.ini`, `AGENTS.md`, `skill/...`, target test file) all present. The destructive commit is NOT an ancestor of `origin/dev` nor of `origin/main` — the remote is clean; the damage is local-only.
- Remaining local references to the destructive commit: branch `dev` and worktree branch `wl-SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK-quality-improvement`.

## Root-cause correlation (strong, not yet proven)

The placeholder filenames and the git identity (`T <t@t.com>`, commit message "init") exactly match the fixture `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` (origin/dev lines ~481, 502, 548): it runs `git init`, sets `user.email t@t.com` / `user.name T`, writes those 5 files + `tests/test_a.py` with "x
", and commits "init". Under some condition (likely in the loaded multi-agent environment) the fixture's git operations ran against the live repo instead of an isolated tmp path, wiping the tree and committing. This is the same class of test-isolation pollution suspected in the failing-test work item SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D.

## Proposed recovery (NEEDS AUTHORISATION — not performed)

1. `git fetch origin` (remote already known-good).
2. Reset the local main checkout: `git checkout -B dev origin/dev` (or `git -c core.bare=false reset --hard origin/dev`) — restores the full tree; untracked files (`.worklog`, `node_modules`, `.pi`, caches) are preserved.
3. Address stale local worktree branch `wl-SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK-quality-improvement` (still contains the destructive commit).
4. Confirmed root cause of the test-isolation failure and fix the fixture so it can never operate outside its tmp dir.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Local `dev` again contains the full repository tree (verified by `ls pytest.ini skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `git status`).
2. The destructive commit `2c30dbfe` is unreachable from any local branch.
3. Root cause of the fixture's escape into the live repo is identified and a test-isolation guard added so `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest` cannot operate on the live repo (e.g. assert tmp isolation before `git init`).
4. Full project test suite passes on the recovered checkout.

## Open Questions

- Authorise local main-checkout reset to `origin/dev`? (Risk: shared checkout, other agents may be mid-operation.)
- Should the fixture change be handled here or via a separate work item?
- Was the destructive commit ever pushed to a shared remote branch other than dev/main (e.g. a PR branch)?

## Problem

The committed git hooks `.githooks/post-checkout` and `.githooks/post-merge` (worklog:post-pull-hook:v1) delegate to the CENTRAL script:

```sh
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

But `~/.config/pi/.githooks/` does not exist on this machine, so EVERY git checkout/merge errors with `exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found` and the post-pull `wl sync` never runs. `scripts/install_pi.sh` only installs the `pre-push` hook into the project `.githooks/` — it does not install the central script, and no other installer creates `~/.config/pi/.githooks/`.

## Evidence

- `cat ~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → No such file or directory (2026-09-19).
- The central script itself is committed in-repo at `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` (runs `wl sync`; skippable via WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1).
- Reproduced during recovery: `.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: ...: not found` after `git checkout`.

## Suggested fix (installer, no code change to hooks)

1. `mkdir -p ~/.config/pi/.githooks`
2. Install a copy/symlink of the repo's `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` there (e.g. `ln -s <repo>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull ~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`).
3. Extend `scripts/install_pi.sh` to do this idempotently so fresh environments don't regress (this part is a repo change → implement work item).
4. Verify: `git checkout` in any repo with these hooks no longer errors and `wl sync` runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists and is executable.
2. A `git checkout`/merge in this repo completes without a hook `not found` error.
3. `scripts/install_pi.sh` idempotently installs the central hook on fresh environments.

## Problem Statement

The test fixture `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` (~lines 481-548) creates a real git repo and runs `git init`, `git add -A`, and `git commit -qm "init"` against `tmp_path`. If `tmp_path`/TMPDIR resolution ever points at a live repository, the fixture stages the ENTIRE repo state and commits an "init" commit that deletes every tracked file except a 6-file placeholder set.

**Incident (2026-09-19):** this occurred during SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK implementation. Running `run_tests.py --scope full` in a worktree produced commit `2c30dbfe` ("init", author T <t@t.com>) that deleted 472 files / 138,009 lines. The corrupted HEAD was pushed to origin/dev (after the pre-push gate was bypassed) before it was detected and force-reverted via `74bd0437`. Damage was recovered; root cause remains unfixed.

## Evidence

- Fixture creates exactly: `install.sh`, `remote`, `sshl`, `update`, `ai.home.conf`, `tests/test_a.py`.
- Commit `2c30dbfe` tree contains exactly those 6 files; author identity T <t@t.com> and message "init" match the fixture exactly.
- `git diff origin/dev..2c30dbfe` = 472 files changed, 138,009 deletions.
- Recovery: origin/dev rewritten to `74bd0437` (fix re-applied); `2c30dbfe` verified NOT an ancestor of origin/dev.

## Suggested Fix Direction

1. Make `_init_repo` defensive: assert `tmp_path` is not inside the repo under test; refuse to run if the resolved path contains `.git` (or if `git -C <repo> rev-parse --show-toplevel` escapes the sandbox).
2. Investigate why `tmp_path`/basetemp resolved to the live repo during the incident (pytest TMPDIR/basetemp handling under the test-skill runner).
3. Add a guard in the fixture (e.g. `if (repo/"..").resolve() == REPO_ROOT: fail`) and a regression test that the fixture never mutates a repo outside the sandbox.
4. Optionally harden the implement/test runners to refuse destructive operations in worktrees (or run tests with a dedicated TMPDIR).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo` can never commit into a repository other than its own tmp dir (guard + regression test).
2. Root-cause of TMPDIR/basetemp misresolution during the incident is documented (or eliminated).
3. Full audit test suite passes.

# Intake Brief: Make it explicit that game scenes should match functionality in the Gym Scenes (or vice-versa)

## Problem statement

The game code is exercised via both real game scenes and Gym Scenes, but there is no explicit guidance ensuring parity between them. Without this, agents may implement gameplay and gym scenes differently, causing divergence that breaks test reliability.

## Users

- **AI agents** implementing game features: need clear guidance on how gym scenes should mirror game scenes.
- **AI agents** writing tests: need to understand the relationship between game scenes and gym scenes when creating or reviewing test files.

## Acceptance Criteria
